objectives: Decode taught sm-words by mapping graphemes from left to right.
Blend the initial sm onset with the vowel and remaining sounds to read the complete word.
Distinguish sm from other taught initial blends without guessing.
Self-correct by checking every grapheme and rereading the complete word.
concepts: Decoding maps written graphemes to sounds in order.
The initial sm onset contains both s and m.
The remaining letters must be decoded rather than guessed.
Rereading checks that all graphemes are represented.

definitions.definition: A letter or group of letters representing a speech sound.
Use grapheme-sound knowledge to read a written word.
Notice an error and repair it using sound and word evidence.

workedExamples.solution: Map s-m-o-g, blend /s/ /m/ /ŏ/ /g/, then say smog.
Keep s and m in order, then read the remaining graphemes to say smile.

workedExamples.prompt: A learner reads smell as sell. What should happen?
workedExamples.solution: Return to the m after s, map each grapheme, and reread smell.
